title: CAC Payback Period Benchmarks by SaaS Stage
summary: CAC payback period benchmark data traced to its source. See the gross-margin-adjusted formula, segment targets, and the ledger setup behind the number.
body_markdown:
## What CAC Payback Period Measures


Every CAC payback period benchmark measures one thing: how many months of gross profit it takes to repay acquisition cost.


It’s a cash-recovery clock, not a profitability test.


That distinction is why indinero rebuilds the number from the general ledger and the billing system instead of reading it off a dashboard. Indinero’s CPA team builds GAAP-compliant books from day one, and payback falls apart the moment expense classification gets loose.


[Benchmarkit](https://www.benchmarkit.ai/2025benchmarks) , which runs the largest recurring B2B SaaS metrics survey, defines the metric in its 2025 SaaS Performance Metrics report as the months needed to pay back sales and marketing expense for new customers on a gross margin adjusted basis. The adjustment isn’t optional. It’s part of the definition.


- **Not a profitability test.**[Bessemer’s Scaling to $100 Million](https://www.bvp.com/atlas/scaling-to-100-million) analysis, published September 21, 2021, is explicit that customers become profitable only after the payback period expires. The metric locates break-even and stops there.
- **Not a cash metric unless you build it that way.**[SaaS Capital’s contracting research](https://www.saas-capital.com/research/how-b2b-saas-companies-price-and-contract/) reports that nearly half of surveyed B2B SaaS companies contract annually and collect the year upfront. Annual prepay recovers the cash on day one and the gross profit over the payback window. Both belong in the board package.
- **Not a single number.** It’s a family, depending on whether the denominator is new-name ARR, expansion ARR, or both.


For a Controller the hard part isn’t the definition. It’s reproducibility. The same figure has to come out of the same accounts next month, which takes three decisions the definition skips: which accounts roll into sales and marketing, how capitalized contract costs are treated, and how new-business spend is split from expansion. Those decisions sit upstream of any[SaaS metrics dashboard](https://www.indinero.com/blog/saas-metrics-dashboard-essentials/) .


## How to Calculate


The CAC payback period formula is lagged sales and marketing expense divided by new ARR times gross margin, multiplied by 12.


Knowing how to calculate CAC payback period is less about that line than about what feeds it.


**Unadjusted:** S&M expense / new ARR added x 12


**Gross-margin-adjusted:** S&M expense / (new ARR added x gross margin %) x 12


[Ben Murray’s definition at The SaaS CFO](https://www.thesaascfo.com/saas-cac-ratio/) , published March 29, 2020 and updated September 25, 2026, is the most specific public list of what fully burdened sales and marketing expense includes:


- Wages, payroll taxes, and benefits for sales and marketing headcount
- Sales commissions
- Travel, conference, and trade show expense
- Paid media, content, and training
- Software and tooling used by the sales and marketing functions


The boundary that does the most damage runs between COGS and sales and marketing, because moving a cost across it changes the numerator and the gross margin divisor at once, in opposite directions.[SaaS Capital’s COGS guidance](https://www.saas-capital.com/blog-posts/what-should-be-included-in-cogs-for-my-saas-business/) keeps sales commissions, amortized development cost, product management, and upsell-focused customer success out of COGS. Account management stays out too. Put it in, and you understate gross margin and lengthen payback for no economic reason.


For a sanity check on the numerator,[SaaS Capital’s 2026 spending benchmarks](https://www.saas-capital.com/blog-posts/spending-benchmarks-for-private-b2b-saas-companies/) , from its 15th annual survey completed in March 2026 with more than 1,000 private B2B SaaS respondents, put median sales spend at 15% of ARR and marketing at 8%. That’s 23% combined. If your S&M sits well under 23% and payback still looks long, the problem is conversion. If it sits well above and payback looks short, check whether capitalized commissions are suppressing the expense line.


None of this reproduces month after month without a department or class dimension on every expense account, which is a[chart of accounts](https://www.indinero.com/blog/chart-of-accounts-for-saas/) decision rather than a reporting decision.


### Gross-Margin-Adjusted Payback, and Why the Unadjusted Number Flatters You


The unadjusted figure always equals the adjusted figure times your gross margin, so it understates recovery time by exactly one minus gross margin.


Take a $12M ARR B2B SaaS company closing Q2, with a 90-day sales cycle and a 78% software gross margin. That 78% sits just under the 80% median software gross margin in Benchmarkit’s full-year 2025 data and inside the 80% to 85% range SaaS Capital reports for license revenue.


- **Fully burdened Q1 S&M expense, lagged one quarter:** $2,400,000
- **New-name ARR closed in Q2:** $1,600,000
- **Unadjusted:** $2,400,000 / $1,600,000 = 1.50, times 12 = **18.0 months**
- **Gross-margin-adjusted:** $1,600,000 x 0.78 = $1,248,000 of new gross profit. $2,400,000 / $1,248,000 = 1.923, times 12 = **23.1 months**


The gap is 5.1 months, or 22%, which is one minus the gross margin. That identity lets you sanity-check any reported payback figure in seconds. If a dashboard says 18 months, your margin is 78%, and nobody can tell you whether the margin was applied, the real range is 18 to 23 months.[ChartMogul’s CAC payback reference](https://chartmogul.com/saas-metrics/cac-payback/) , updated September 8, 2026, gives the reason in one line: you only recover cash from the margin you keep.


At 18.0 months this company looks like it sits inside the segment target Bessemer publishes for mid-market-focused companies. At 23.1 months it doesn’t.


Same ledger, same quarter, one divisor.


### The Sales-Cycle Lag, and Which Direction the Error Runs


[CJ Gustafson at Mostly Metrics](https://www.mostlymetrics.com/p/how-to-calculate-customer-acquisition) gives the most specific public guidance on timing. Lag sales and marketing expense by the length of the sales cycle, because the dollars that closed this quarter’s ARR were largely spent earlier.


Motion Average sales cycle S&M lag


Enterprise 180 days 2 quarters


Mid-market 90 days 1 quarter


SMB or self-serve 30 days 0 quarters


One detail most write-ups miss. You don’t lag COGS or gross margin. Only the numerator moves.


Competing content asserts that lagging always makes payback look worse. That holds only for flat or falling spend. Continue the example with Q2 S&M of $2,760,000, a 15% increase over Q1. Unlagged and adjusted, payback is 26.5 months. Lagged one quarter, 23.1. For a company increasing spend, the unlagged number overstates payback by 3.4 months, because this quarter’s larger spend hasn’t produced bookings yet. For a company that just cut spend, the arithmetic reverses and the unlagged number flatters. That’s the dangerous case, since the quarter after a cut is when management most wants a good number.


A lag applied only in good quarters is a reporting artifact, not a metric.


### Blended, New-Name, and Paid CAC


Blended CAC ratio divides total S&M by new plus expansion ARR. New-name divides new-business S&M by new customer ARR. Murray’s fallback, where the ledger can’t separate the spend, is the headcount ratio between new-logo and existing-account reps.


[Maxio’s summary of the 2025 B2B SaaS Performance Metrics Benchmark Report](https://www.maxio.com/blog/2025-saas-benchmark-report-trends) , produced with Benchmarkit across more than 500 B2B SaaS companies on full-year 2024 data, puts the blended CAC ratio at $1.40, improved 13% from $1.61, and the new CAC ratio at $2.00, worsened from $1.76. Report blended payback only, and you’re describing the health of the installed base as if it were the health of new customer acquisition.


That pair also exposes a reconciliation gap. Since payback months equal the CAC ratio divided by gross margin times 12, $1.40 at an 80% median gross margin implies roughly 21 months, which doesn’t reconcile with the 18-month FY2024 median that circulates for the same dataset. Different respondent subsets is the likely answer, because not every respondent reports every metric. Don’t mix medians across metrics from one survey and treat the result as one coherent company.


Paid CAC narrows the numerator to direct paid acquisition spend. Useful for channel decisions, useless for payback, because salaries, commissions, events, and content are most of what it excludes. Running both views side by side is a[BI reporting](https://www.indinero.com/services/technology-business-intelligence-services/) build, not a spreadsheet.


### Capitalized Commissions, and Why GAAP S&M Isn’t What You Spent


Under ASC 340-40-25-1, an entity is required to recognize as an asset the incremental costs of obtaining a contract with a customer when it expects to recover them, and the codification’s own example of such a cost is a sales commission.[PwC’s Viewpoint reference on costs to obtain a contract](https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/fasb_financial_accou/trg_revenue/trg_revenue_US/incremental_costs_of__1_US.html) states the test as costs the entity wouldn’t have incurred had the contract not been obtained. Capitalization isn’t a policy election. ASC 340-40-25-4 supplies the only out, a practical expedient to expense as incurred when the amortization period would be one year or less.


Those periods often run far past the contract term.[Workday’s August 8, 2017 correspondence with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1327811/000119312517251705/filename1.htm) documents five-year amortization of capitalized commissions even though its subscription contracts generally run three years or longer, reflecting average contract term plus anticipated renewals, the rate of technological change, and renewal commissions far lower than initial ones.


- Reported S&M in any period includes amortization of commissions from prior-period contracts and excludes the part of this period’s commissions that was capitalized.
- For a company growing bookings, capitalization suppresses current-period S&M and makes payback look shorter than the cash reality.
- Keep two numbers. GAAP payback is what an auditor and an acquirer tie to, cash payback is what the forecast needs, and the reconciling item is the movement in the contract cost asset. Same discipline[ASC 606](https://www.indinero.com/blog/asc-606-what-you-need-to-know/) already demanded of the revenue side.


## Benchmarks by Stage


CAC payback by stage is the framing everyone wants, and it’s the one the public record supports least. Segment and contract value drive the number.


So what’s a good CAC payback period SaaS companies at your stage actually hit? Benchmarkit, working from more than 500 B2B SaaS companies on full-year 2024 data, reports the metric is most instructive viewed by annual contract value, which has the highest correlation to its value, and that deals above $250K ACV pay back materially faster than the $50K to $100K and $25K to $50K bands. The worst payback sits in the middle of the ACV range, not at the top. Benchmarkit also cautions that common wisdom says roughly 12 months is good while the metric is highly correlated to ACV. The publisher of the largest recurring survey is warning you off the 12-month rule.


Bessemer’s September 2021 segment targets are the most defensible prescriptive set available. They come from Bessemer’s own portfolio of more than 200 cloud investments covering 2010 through the first half of 2021, with an explicit footnote that this is not a random sample of the entire private market. Bessemer notes that segment type matters more than ARR scale.


Segment Published target Observed figure, publisher and sample


Self-serve or product-led Under 12 months (practitioner guidance) No primary survey figure located


SMB-focused, low ACV Under 12 months (Bessemer, 2021) Lower payback at low ACV than mid-range, direction only (Benchmarkit, 500+ companies, FY2024)


Mid-market-focused Under 18 months (Bessemer, 2021) $25K to $100K ACV is the worst band (Benchmarkit, FY2024)


Enterprise-focused, $250K-plus ACV Under 24 months (Bessemer, 2021) Faster than the $50K to $100K band (Benchmarkit, FY2024)


Public software Not applicable About 20 months adjusted, almost 100 public companies ([Benchmarkit](https://www.benchmarkit.ai/) , 2023)


Bessemer’s one observed stage figure is a 15-month average for the $1M to $10M ARR bucket, from that same non-random portfolio. For full-year 2025, Benchmarkit confirms on its own site that CAC payback improved 11% year over year across 342 B2B SaaS and AI-native software companies. A 16-month median appears in[Aleph’s summary](https://www.getaleph.com/answers/cac-payback-period-saas-2026) of that June 1, 2026 report, but the absolute figure sits behind a gated download. Treat the 16 as a co-publisher figure, not a publisher figure. That care is why indinero footnotes benchmark attribution in every[SaaS board package](https://www.indinero.com/industries/saas-accounting-services/) it builds.


### Figures This Page Won’t Repeat, and Why


Seven figure families circulate as CAC payback benchmarks. None survived a source check.


- **The Series-stage table.** Bootstrapped 4.8 months, Series A 10 to 12, Series B 14 to 18, Series C+ 18 to 24. It runs across multiple 2026 aggregator pages with no publisher, no report title, and no year.
- **“939 companies.”** No publisher, no report, no year.
- **The product-led set.** A 4.2-month median, $702 self-serve CAC, $11,400 sales-led CAC, and a “16x gap.” No primary source. The defensible version is[practitioner guidance from Benchmarkit and OpenView](https://www.benchmarkit.ai/metrics-that-measure-up-podcasts/product-led-growth-metrics-and-benchmarks) that under 12 months is great for self-serve.
- **KeyBanc medians of 24, 14, and 18 months.** The October 23, 2024 and[November 13, 2025](https://investor.key.com/press-releases/news-details/2025/PRIVATE-SAAS-COMPANY-SURVEY-REVEALS-AI-DRIVEN-TRANSFORMATION-AND-SUSTAINED-OPERATIONAL-EXCELLENCE/default.aspx) releases with Sapphire Ventures publish growth, retention, and quota attainment. Neither publishes a CAC payback median. The 2025 release projects account executive payback shortening to 18 months by 2026, a different metric and almost certainly where the confusion started.
- **The 15 to 16 month “market median.”** Two traceable origins, neither a representative survey. Bessemer’s 15 months is the portfolio average above. ChartMogul’s CAC payback page carries two illustrative examples that land at 15 and 16 months, and those are hypotheticals.
- **The sub-12-month “healthy range.”** It traces to[David Skok’s SaaS Metrics 2.0](https://www.forentrepreneurs.com/saas-metrics-2/) , which says the best SaaS businesses recover CAC in 5 to 7 months and profitability is anemic beyond 12. No sample, no survey, no year. Every verifiable observed figure above sits over 12 months.
- **The 12-month threshold borrowed from B2C.**[Stripe’s reference page](https://stripe.com/resources/more/what-is-the-cac-payback-period) , last updated September 10, 2024, anchors 12 months to B2C and notes B2B can exceed it. The qualifier gets stripped on the way into B2B tables, next to ecommerce at under 3 months. Those aren’t points on one distribution.


## What Drives CAC Payback Variance


Annual contract value explains more CAC payback variance than funding stage or ARR does, and the relationship isn’t linear.


- **ACV, with a non-linear shape.** Benchmarkit’s 2024 dataset puts the worst payback mid-range. The $25K to $100K band is the squeeze, too large for self-serve conversion and too small to justify an enterprise motion. Funnel work doesn’t fix a structural position.
- **Gross margin, a direct multiplier.** Moving from 85% to 75% lengthens payback by 13% with no change in acquisition spend. Companies carrying heavy professional services inside COGS read payback against their own margin, not the 80% median.
- **Expansion mix.**[Benchmarkit’s 2026 SaaS and AI-Native Metrics](https://www.benchmarkit.ai/2026-saas-ai-native-metrics) , covering 342 companies on full-year 2025 actuals, reports expansion supplying 40% of net new ARR at median. That’s the mechanism behind the $1.40 and $2.00 gap.
- **Pricing model.** The same report splits net revenue retention at 108% for usage-based against 98% for seat-based. Usage-based defers revenue into the post-acquisition period, which lengthens first-year payback.
- **Funding posture.** SaaS Capital’s March 2026 survey of more than 1,000 private B2B SaaS companies reports equity-backed companies spending 70% more on sales and 100% more on marketing than bootstrapped ones.
- **Quota attainment.** The[15th annual KeyBanc and Sapphire private SaaS survey](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/private-saas-company-survey-reveals-shift-towards-future-growth-with-a-continued-focus-on-operational-efficiency-and-profitability-302284711.html) from October 2024, covering more than 100 private SaaS companies with median 2023 ARR of about $26M, reports attainment rising from roughly 70% to roughly 75%. Below-plan attainment leaves rep cost in the numerator without the ARR.


CAC payback answers how fast acquisition spend returns, while[burn multiple](https://www.indinero.com/blog/burn-multiple-by-saas-stage/) answers how much total cash a dollar of net new ARR consumed, and the two are complements rather than substitutes.


## How to Improve CAC Payback Period


The fastest way to improve CAC payback period is to stop computing it wrong, because a blended, unlagged, unadjusted number points at the wrong lever.


1. **Fix the denominator before touching the spend.** Split new-name ARR from expansion ARR and compute both ratios. The $1.40 against $2.00 spread is the size of the error this corrects at median.
2. **Apply the gross margin divisor and the lag permanently.** Good quarters and bad, with the convention documented. At an 80% margin, an unadjusted figure understates payback by 20% every month.
3. **Clean the COGS classification.** Moving upsell-focused customer success out of COGS and into expansion sales cost lifts gross margin and correctly loads the expansion ratio. No price increase required.
4. **Commit on ACV instead of drifting into the middle.** Push down toward self-serve price points, where Benchmarkit and OpenView guidance says under 12 months is great, or up to where enterprise contract value carries the sales cost.


The middle is the expensive place to sit.
5. **Shorten the sales cycle.** It cuts fully loaded cost per deal and pulls the repaying gross profit forward.
6. **Shift mix toward expansion, with the tradeoff in view.** Expansion ARR carries a far lower acquisition cost, and usage-based pricing defers revenue into later periods.
7. **Use annual prepay for the cash problem payback is a proxy for.** It doesn’t change the accounting number. It changes when the cash arrives, which is usually the real constraint.
8. **Raise quota attainment before raising headcount.** Hiring into a sub-plan attainment rate lengthens payback mechanically.
9. **Cross-check against magic number.** Benchmarkit’s full-year 2025 data puts the median magic number above 1.0 for the first time in years. If payback improved and magic number didn’t, that’s a mix shift or a measurement change, not an efficiency gain.


Levers 1, 3, and 8 are ledger and process work, which is why they land with whoever runs the close and the[FP&A cycle](https://www.indinero.com/blog/outsourced-fpa-services/) rather than with the growth team.


## How Indinero Builds CAC Payback Into Reporting


Indinero rebuilds CAC payback from your general ledger and billing data, then puts the trend into monthly board reporting.


There’s no dashboard product behind that, because indinero sells no software and stays tool-neutral. Subscription analytics platforms hold no expense data, so they compute ARPA, retention, and expansion from billing records alone. CAC payback is the one metric that needs the ledger and the billing system joined, which is why[published benchmark libraries](https://chartmogul.com/reports/) covering growth, retention, and plan mix carry no CAC payback benchmark.


The work is close-process work, not dashboard configuration:


- **Department and class structure** on the chart of accounts, so sales, marketing, customer success, and professional services separate every month without a judgment call.
- **Separate commission accounts** for new business and for expansion or renewal, which removes the allocation estimate from the new-name ratio.
- **An ASC 340-40 contract cost asset schedule** maintained monthly with the practical expedient decision documented, since[PwC’s Viewpoint guidance](https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/fasb_financial_accou/trg_revenue/trg_revenue_US/capitalization_and_a_US.html) requires capitalization unless the amortization period is one year or less.
- **COGS classification reviewed at the boundary cases** , specifically account management, upsell-focused customer success, and amortized development cost.
- **A documented lag convention** applied every period, so the board-package trend is comparable quarter to quarter.
- **Both numbers in the package.** GAAP payback for the auditors and any future acquirer, cash payback for the forecast, with the bridge shown.

## Frequently asked questions


A few questions come up every time a payback number lands in a board package. Here’s how we answer them.


### Which costs belong in CAC, and which ones do not?


Fully loaded sales and marketing expense for acquiring new customers belongs in CAC, while customer success, account management, and anything in COGS stay out. Fully loaded means wages, payroll taxes, benefits, commissions, paid media, events, and the software those two functions use. Indinero puts a department and class dimension on every expense account, since the COGS boundary is where misclassification moves the numerator and the gross margin divisor at once, in opposite directions.


### Should CAC payback use gross profit or revenue?


CAC payback should use gross profit, dividing sales and marketing expense by new ARR times gross margin rather than by revenue alone. The unadjusted figure always equals the adjusted figure times gross margin, which is exactly why the revenue version flatters you. At a 78% gross margin, an 18.0-month unadjusted read becomes 23.1 months adjusted, and that identity lets you sanity-check any payback number in seconds.


### What is a good CAC payback period for a Series A SaaS company?


No credible Series A CAC payback benchmark exists in the public record, and the stage tables in circulation have no named publisher. Segment and contract value drive the number, not funding stage. Bessemer’s September 2021 segment targets, from its own portfolio of more than 200 cloud investments and explicitly not a random market sample, put SMB-focused companies under 12 months, mid-market under 18, and enterprise under 24.


### Why does CAC payback look worse the faster we grow?


Fast growth loads new sales and marketing spend into the numerator before the bookings it buys close, so unlagged CAC payback overstates recovery time. The fix is to lag sales and marketing expense by your sales cycle, two quarters for enterprise, one for mid-market, none for self-serve. Competing guidance claims lagging always worsens payback, but that holds only for flat or falling spend, and after a cut the unlagged number flatters instead.


### Where do blended CAC and paid CAC diverge?


Blended CAC includes organic and self-serve acquisition while paid CAC isolates spend-driven acquisition, so the two diverge most when organic is strong. Paid CAC is useful for channel decisions and useless for payback, because salaries, commissions, events, and content are most of what it excludes. Blended CAC ratio carries its own risk, dividing total spend by new plus expansion ARR, which Benchmarkit data puts at $1.40 against $2.00 for new customers alone.


### Can CAC payback be calculated monthly, or is it a quarterly metric?


CAC payback can be computed monthly, but the read is noisy, so a trailing-three-month or quarterly view is the more reliable board number. The sales-cycle lag means a single month’s spend rarely matches the ARR it produced, and a small new-ARR denominator swings hard on one large or one slipped deal. Indinero computes it monthly for trend and reports the trailing three months in the board package, with the lag convention documented so good quarters and bad use the same one.


### Does CAC payback work for a product-led company with no sales team?


CAC payback works for a product-led company, with marketing and self-serve acquisition cost as the numerator and new ARR times gross margin below it. The sales-cycle lag drops to zero because self-serve conversion is near-immediate, which is the one simplification product-led motions get. Practitioner guidance from Benchmarkit and OpenView says under 12 months is great for self-serve, and the circulating product-led medians and self-serve CAC figures have no primary publisher behind them, so don’t plan against them.
